heading: INT. STARLITE ROLLER RINK - AFTER HOURS

units.text: INT. STARLITE ROLLER RINK - AFTER HOURS
A cavern of scuffed maple and dead disco light.
A mirror ball turns slowly, throwing coins of silver across the walls.
The air smells of popcorn oil, rubber wheels, and thirty years of cheap perfume.
ODALYS FERREIRA, 50s, in a faded satin jacket that says STARLITE STAFF, stands at the center of the floor with a push broom.
She has been sweeping the same square of wood for some time.
At the skate counter, FITZ MCALLISTER, 60s, owner, sorts a bin of rental skates by size.
He doesn't look up.
A mug of coffee steams beside a signed contract.
BASHIR KARIMI, 30s, a suit too good for this building, leans against the DJ booth with a briefcase.
JUNIPER FERREIRA, 17, headphones around her neck, sits on the rail with her skates in her lap, pretending to lace them.
Mrs. Ferreira, I don't want to rush anyone. But the buyer needs the keys by Friday.
units.name: BASHIR

units.text: I heard you the first time.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: She heard you.
units.name: FITZ

units.text: Thirty-one years I've swept this floor.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: And the new development will keep a plaque --
units.name: BASHIR

units.text: A plaque.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: Mom.
units.name: JUNIPER

units.text: Don't "Mom" me. You learned to walk on this floor.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: I learned to fall on this floor.
units.name: JUNIPER

units.text: Fitz puts down a skate.
Laughs once, softly.
Then louder.
Then it turns into something else.
He covers his face.
I signed it, Odie. Tuesday. I couldn't tell you.
units.name: FITZ

units.text: The broom drops.
It clatters across the maple, a flat hollow sound that rings up into the rafters.
You what.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: The roof is gone. The boiler is gone. I've been paying the electric with my pension --
units.name: FITZ

units.text: YOU DIDN'T ASK ME.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: Please, let's all just take a breath --
units.name: BASHIR

units.text: Get out.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: Get out.
units.name: JUNIPER

units.text: Bashir picks up his briefcase and, for once, is quick about it.
The glass door closes behind him with a polite chime.
The mirror ball keeps turning.
Odalys sits down hard on the floor.
Fitz comes around the counter and sits beside her, knees creaking.
Neither speaks.
Juniper stands.
Laces her skates properly this time.
She rolls out onto the empty rink, slow, then faster, and loops the whole oval alone.
She's got your father's stride.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: She's got yours.
units.name: FITZ

units.text: Odalys wipes her cheek with the heel of her hand.
Then stands, offers Fitz a hand up.
He takes it.
Put on the Bee Gees.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: We're closed.
units.name: FITZ

units.text: Put on the Bee Gees, Fitzgerald.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: He crosses to the booth.
Taps a button.
A bass line thumps out of tired speakers.
The silver light sweeps the three of them as Juniper glides past, arms out, laughing.
